title.narrative: Addressing drivers of conflict, and promoting the fulfilment of human rights, sustainable governance of natural resources, climate justice and environmental protection through evidence based research and grassroots collaboration.

description.narrative: Contract related to: Addressing drivers of conflict, and promoting the fulfilment of human rights, sustainable governance of natural resources, climate justice and environmental protection through evidence based research and grassroots collaboration. - The action will focus in particular on three major goals. The first on is the continued support to the Regional Approach to the Mano River belt region of West Africa (Sierra Leone, Liberia, Guinea Conakry, Cote d¿Ivoire) to strengthen the implementation of the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS) in the Mano River Union at the regional and national level. A regional approach to policy discourse on issues such as smuggling, ways to improve the livelihood conditions for mining communities while simultaneously increasing the space and roles for civil society in the mining sector has proven to be successful. With this action, the aim is to pave the way for its potential replication in Central Africa as well. As a second objective, the action will continue engaging, empowering and equipping civil society's active participation in the Kimberley Process (KP) and other due diligence initiatives. The action¿s third goal is to raise awareness of environmental management in mining governance in the selected regions and encourage locally led, conflict sensitive environmental degradation mitigating activities, in particular with artisanal and alluvial miners. Finally, the development of new technologies and shift to green, renewable way of life increases demands for the critical raw materials that power the green transition. The action will support research and dialogue to ensure better understanding of risks of destructive conflict caused or exacerbated by mining for green transition, in particular in conflict-prone and vulnerable countries and regions, such as West and Central Africa.

comment.narrative: Building on its research and capacity enhancement in Phase 1 of this action IPIS continues to address specific drivers for armed conflict and work with key stakeholders to tackle them. This action focusses on natural resources governance illicit trade in natural resources and climate change stand as key conflict drivers. Addressing these conflict drivers requires a multilateral approach.This multilateral and even multistakeholder approach is largely in place for the focal topics of this action for instance in addressing climate change due diligence or diamond trade within the Kimberley Process context. IPIS research and collaboration with partners at grassroots level aims to inform and strengthen existing multilateral fora and promote regional cooperation to respond to existing or emerging crises.

IPIS analyses the underlying political economy of conflict in order to identify the powerholders that influence economic engagement on a local national and global level and target them for change. These power holders can be incountry authorities local war lords private enterprises and states as economic actors and regulatory bodies. Power holders can exert negative influence but can also be or become positive forces for change to the benefit of communities.With its research and through its partnerships IPIS aims to contribute to durable peace sustainable development and human rights. IPIS and its partners work with local national international and multilateral stakeholders to improve practice policy and legislation so that communities benefit rather than suffer from the exploitation of their natural resources. The element of change we envisage is that policy makers governments and industry base legislation policies and practices on evidencebased research.To make this change coherent requires a multilateral approach.

Improving diamond governance in an effective and sustainable manner requires a better understanding of the good and bad practices stumbling blocks spoilers and opportunities on both the specific countryregionallevel and the global sectorwidescale. IPIS research capacity enhancement and policy work on diamonds will therefore take a twopronged approach with close interlinkages between the two components.For the first component IPIS will strategically select country or regionallevel cases to study and improve the impact of diamond mining on stability human security and socio economic advancement. In this strand IPIS will work in close partnership with and build capacities of incountry CSOs from the Kimberley Process Civil Society Coalition KP CSC or other CSO networks. The findings will feed into national and international policy discussions such as for instance KP meetings working groups and review visits.In the second component IPIS will zoom out and tackle the bigger questions that face the diamond industry globally. IPIS will closely follow the dynamics and discussions within the industry and multilateral fora in order to select those questions that are most pertinent and pressing to address. Both components of this approach will be closely interlinked and mutually reinforce each other. The countryregionlevel experiences will provide the reality check in answering the bigger policy questions while these bigger frameworks will help guide and give direction to the targeted contextual work.Outputs CSO partners in diamond producing countries are able to enhance their monitoring and reporting capacities and improve their visibility recognition and impact visvis governmental and corporate stakeholdersStakeholders involved in national and international policymaking fora better understand the impact of natural resource governance on human security and developmentCorporate governmental and civil society stakeholders have access to and use practical guides to overcome the main challenges in ensuring a conflictsensitive management of diamond resources.

IPIS research capacity enhancement and policy work on diamonds will therefore take a twopronged approach with close interlinkages between the two components.For the first component IPIS will strategically select country or regionallevel cases to study and improve the impact of diamond mining on stability human security and socio economic advancement. In this strand IPIS will work in close partnership with and build capacities of incountry CSOs from the Kimberley Process Civil Society Coalition KP CSC or other CSO networks. The findings will feed into national and international policy discussions such as for instance KP meetings working groups and review visits.In the second component IPIS will zoom out and tackle the bigger questions that face the diamond industry globally. IPIS will closely follow the dynamics and discussions within the industry and multilateral fora in order to select those questions that are most pertinent and pressing to address. Both components of this approach will be closely interlinked and mutually reinforce each other. description.narrative: Number of Civil Society Organisations representatives trained on responsible business conduct standards for conflict minerals and extraction of other natural resources (M/W)

comment.narrative: The action aims at building a coalition with common objectives to optimize the impact of the instrument and the capacity to successfully address or resolve incidents including on irresponsible business conduct. This requires exchange common strategizing and a governance structure to address reported incidents at the appropriate level local through the partner CSOs regional and national or supranational through the coalition. Baseline No trainingYear 1 CSOs trained in Lualaba on CMR CRMA Battery Regulation exchange in annual Kufatilia meetingYear 2 continued follow up of Kufatilia incidents implementation of Kufatilia action plan and training and planning of a Kufatilia workshop at the start of year 3.

As a network regrouping 25 CSOs and counting Kufatilia acts as a de facto coalition of civil society organizations active in the mining sector in HautUele Ituri North and SouthKivu and Lualaba starting in 2022. While the option to expand the network to other organizations and to other provinces in the DRC is always a possibility the current and urgent needs would be to strengthen this network to turn it into a coalition of likeminded organisations thus strengthening their voices and positions defending the formalisation of the ASM sector and the rights of the mining communities.To do so IPIS will organize joint training to strengthen coalition members in their role following up on incidents. Its important indeed to keep in mind that incident reporting is only the first step and risks to be affected by reporting fatigue if no actions are taken to follow up remedy and resolve the incidents that are being reported by the mining communities.

comment.narrative: IPIS aims to publish 10 reports 20 IPIS briefings and 10 Voices publication within the timeframe and budget of this action. In both its own and joint projects IPIS wants to strategically and regularly assessengagement opportunities to ensure that findings and recommendations are shared in the most effective ways reach targeted audiences and encourage relevant stakeholders to act upon them. The process will include regular exchange sessions on communication with local civil society partners. Together with them IPIS will identify communication and advocacy gaps and codevelop dissemination and engagement strategies to support advocacy for positive changes for the rights of frontline communities.IPIS will continue to promote its own and joint research findings and recommendations via diverse social media channels but will continuously aim to increase its engagement rate based on the recommendations provided by the communication bureau.IPIS new social media strategy will gravitate around the broadcasting of community based reporting and will amplify grassroots perspectives via audiovisual and derivative products. While defining its new strategy IPIS will explore the potential of Instagram for its storytelling objectives.

description.narrative: This outcome focusses on strengthening the capacities and impact of both the Kimberley Process Civil Society Coalition (KP CSC) and its individual member organisations, which are with the exception of IPIS African NGOs from 11 different countries. The KP CSC is the civil society watchdog in the Kimberley Process (KP). While the KP CSC will continue pushing for meaningful reform within the KP, it will complement this more intensively with its unique role of combining grassroots support and monitoring with policy advice on the national and regional level as well as in various international fora. The latter include multilateral and multistakeholder platforms like the United Nations, African Union, OECD minerals forum, Intergovernmental Forum (IGF) on Mining, and the Alternative Mining Indaba, but also direct industry engagement.

comment.narrative: In order to improve the functioning of the KP CSC information sharing and cooperation at multilateral level at EU and UN level is crucial to secure that the conflict prevention aspect of the Kimberley Process is safeguarded. IPIS and the KP CSC already provide information from a grassroots perspective to inform the EU and exchanges with other multilateral organizations within the UN and multistakeholderplatforms such as the EU. No actions taken in this phase 2 of the action but the KPCSC will build on its results in phase 1 to sustain the existing exchange with multilateral actors.

The action aims at improving and strengthening information sharing and coordination at multilateral level to respond to analysis and reports from the grassroots level. IPIS facilitates this information sharing from the KP Civil Society Coalition. IPIS aims at strengthening its incident reporting network Kufatilia to make sure that reported incidents bring a grassroots perspective to policy and legislation at multilateral level. Information sharing and coordination already exists but will be strengthened by this action.

description.narrative: This outcome focusses on strengthening the capacities and impact of both the Kimberley Process Civil Society Coalition (KP CSC) and its individual member organisations, which are with the exception of IPIS African NGOs from 11 different countries. The KP CSC is the civil society watchdog in the Kimberley Process (KP). While the KP CSC will continue pushing for meaningful reform within the KP, it will complement this more intensively with its unique role of combining grassroots support and monitoring with policy advice on the national and regional level as well as in various international fora. The latter include multilateral and multistakeholder platforms like the United Nations, African Union, OECD minerals forum, Intergovernmental Forum (IGF) on Mining, and the Alternative Mining Indaba, but also direct industry engagement.
